chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jaham, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the most superior place in the Masjid to be prayed in. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Hateem, what is between the Stone and the Door of the House.' I said, 'And that which follows that in superiority?' So he mentioned that it was by the Standing Place of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). I said, 'Then which (spot) follows it in superiority?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'By the Stone.' I said, 'Then which (spot) follows that?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Every (spot) that is closest to the House.'

key_terms.الْحَجَرُ: The Stone (referring to the Black Stone)
key_terms.الْحَطِيمُ: Al-Hateem, the semi-circular wall adjacent to the Kaaba
key_terms.الْحِجْرُ: Al-Hijr, the area enclosed by the semi-circular wall

ai.seo_question: What is the most virtuous place to pray in the Kaaba according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes a precise spatial hierarchy for prayer merit within the Sacred Masjid, identifying the Al-Hateem (the semi-circular wall adjacent to the Kaaba) as the most superior spot due to its inclusion within the Kaaba's structure. The narration further clarifies that merit increases progressively as one approaches the Kaaba itself, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical proximity to the House of God as a means of spiritual elevation. This grading underscores the theological significance of the Kaaba not merely as a focal point (Qibla) but as a locus of divine presence where specific architectural elements hold distinct spiritual weight.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jaham who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> about the most superior place in the Masjid to be Prayed in. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘الْحَطِيمُ’ ‘Al-Hateem, what is between the (Black) Stone and the Door of the House (Kabah)’. I said, ‘And that which follows that in superiority?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned that it was by the Standing Place of Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>’. I said, ‘Then which (spot) follows it in superiority?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By the (Black) Stone’. I said, ‘Then which (spot) follows that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Every (spot) what is closest to the House (Kabah)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the most excellent place for salat (prayer) in Masjid al-Haram (the Sacred Masjid). He (the Imam) replied, ’It is al-Hatim, between the Black Stone and the door of the house.’ I then asked, ‘Which place is excellent thereafter?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is Maqam of Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam .’ I then asked which one is excellent thereafter?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is inside al-Hijr.’ I then asked, ‘Which is excellent thereafter?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Whichever is closer to the House.’”
